messages.text: I’ll inspect the engine brief, issue details, and existing Python semantic-model patterns first. Then I’ll implement the highest-leverage facts and validate the changed surface, keeping the handback report within the required limit.

The issue is a broad fact-completeness lane with several independent gaps. Existing Python facts already cover hierarchy, lifecycle, iterator returns, signatures, and documentation, so I’m tracing the fact producers and RQL filter path before extending those shared surfaces. The lifecycle “nonTrivial” fact remains the first milestone because it addresses four rules at once.

The first high-value capability is now wired: lifecycle rows expose whether the resolved target body contains meaningful statements, with `pass` and docstring-only bodies classified as trivial; unavailable bodies keep the fact open. I also registered the existing special-method status as a filterable RQL field and added regression coverage for both changes. I’m compiling these slices now.

The initial test command stopped before compiling because the long `TMPDIR` made mbx’s Unix socket path exceed the platform limit. I’m retrying with the same mandated scratch location under a short `4645` subdirectory; the format check is still occupying a build slot, so I’m checking that process as well.

The focused run is compiling the Python-enabled integration target from a cold worktree build, so it is taking longer than the socket failure. The format check found only layout changes in the files I touched; I’ll apply those mechanically after the compile finishes, then continue with inherited comparison/member facts and iterator identity.

The issue’s earlier policy trials confirm the exposed `special_method_status` was the RQL filter gap, and the CodeQL sources make the lifecycle behavior explicit. I’m preserving incomplete results when method source cannot be parsed instead of letting the new `target_non_trivial` filter treat that case as clean. The cold test build is still active.

I’m continuing the Python class-member facts implementation. The focused regression build is still compiling; I’ll finish that run, then close the remaining fact gaps, author the requested policy evidence, and validate against the current branch.

The fact wiring has a small first-pass slice in place: lifecycle rows can carry the resolved base method’s triviality, and `special_method_status` is now a registered field. I also found the current `mro_members` provider intentionally returns only C3-selected members, so I’m preserving that contract while separating any completeness gaps into additional typed facts.

The focused policy test is queued behind other lanes’ cold compiles; it has not reached test execution yet. While that builds, I’m using the CodeQL sources to keep the lifecycle predicate aligned with `nonTrivial` (including pure same-name delegation), and I’m preparing separate policy artifacts for the assigned report.

The current build has compiled the changed RQL crate and caught one mechanical warning: a duplicated `special_method_status` projection arm. I’m letting the queued focused test finish first, then I’ll remove that duplicate and add the remaining read/return identity facts with hardwon regressions.

The focused run finished: the lifecycle fact regression passes. The signature filter test exposed a query literal type mismatch (`too_few` was sent as a string for an enum field); I’ll switch it to the enum literal, remove the duplicate projection arm, and rerun both cases. The cold build took 29m42s.

The first focused run exposed one incorrect test filter encoding; I fixed it. The retest is still queued behind the shared Rust build slots, so I’m using that wait to finish the remaining policy candidates and documentation, then I’ll validate the combined changes and hand back the evidence.

The implementation review found two parity gaps before the queued run starts: call-argument receiver reads were checking the wrong tree-sitter node kind, and lifecycle triviality also needs CodeQL’s reachable normal-exit condition. I’m correcting both and extending the regression fixture to cover receiver-as-argument.

The queued retest reached compilation and found four Rust errors in this lane’s changes. I’m collecting the diagnostics now and will fix them before another validation run. The pack-authoring drift check passed, and I fetched the current upstream head for the required merge.

The fact and filter work is now documented, and I added candidate policy files for iterator protocol, special-method signatures, and missing method docstrings in the report area. The retest has acquired a build slot and is compiling the affected RQL crate; I’m waiting for that result before touching source again.
